title: Attention-Aligned Reasoning for Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2510.03223v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) tend to generate a long reasoning chain when solving complex tasks. However, as the reasoning chain extends, critical intermediate steps and the original prompt will be buried in the context, receiving insufficient attention and leading to errors. In this work, we present ATAR, a novel reasoning method that leverages the inherent reasoning structure to steer LLM attention. Our experiments show that ATAR outperforms SOTA methods across six benchmarks, achieving up to 15.39% absolute improvement. Furthermore, with ATAR, "non-reasoning" models achieve comparable or even better performance compared to reasoning models of the same size in most benchmarks. Finally, our ablation studies show that the attention alignment component contributes significantly, and that these improvements are persist under different attentionsteering backends.

translated_title: 大语言模型的注意力对齐推理
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在解决复杂任务时往往会生成长推理链。然而，随着推理链的延伸，关键的中间步骤和原始提示词会被埋没在上下文中，得不到足够的注意力，从而导致错误。在本工作中，我们提出了ATAR，这是一种新颖的推理方法，它利用固有的推理结构来引导大语言模型的注意力。我们的实验表明，ATAR在六个基准测试中优于最先进（SOTA）方法，实现了高达15.39%的绝对提升。此外，借助ATAR，“非推理”模型在大多数基准测试中取得了与同规模推理模型相当甚至更好的性能。最后，我们的消融研究表明，注意力对齐组件贡献显著，且这些改进在不同的注意力引导后端下均能保持。
tldr: 提出了ATAR推理方法，通过利用固有推理结构引导大语言模型的注意力，避免关键中间步骤和原始提示被埋没，在六个基准测试中最高实现15.39%的绝对提升，并使非推理模型达到与同规模推理模型相当甚至更好的性能。
en_tdlr: ATAR is a novel reasoning method that leverages the inherent reasoning structure to steer LLM attention toward critical intermediate steps and original prompts, achieving up to 15.39% absolute improvement over SOTA across six benchmarks and enabling non-reasoning models to match or exceed the performance of similarly-sized reasoning models.
